messages:
Sam K: Hey support — AcmeOps reporting a sudden spike in 502/SSL errors from their private VPC right after our cert rotation at 02:10 UTC. App pods seeing handshake failures.
Priya R: Can you paste the errors? 502 vs SSL come from different layers.
AcmeOps: Logs show: "TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: handshake failure" and our ALB shows 502 from 10.2.3.4:443. Started immediately after rotation.
Sam K: Pulled the rotator job events — job finished but uploaded a smaller bundle than prior ones. Rotator logs: "uploaded cert bundle (size=3.2KB)"; previous bundles ~8.4KB.
Jeff L: Sounds like a truncated bundle (missing intermediate). Can you run an openssl s_client from a node inside their VPC to inspect the chain?
AcmeOps: Ran `openssl s_client -connect api.private.acme.internal:443 -showcerts` — output: "Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.private.acme.internal
 1 s:/CN=Acme Intermediate CA" — then only printed the leaf, not the cross-signed intermediate. `curl -v` shows weird bits: "SSL: certificate subject name 'api.private.acme.internal' matched
* subjectAltNames: host name 'api.private.acme.internal' matched
* SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches"
Priya R: That curl output is odd — could be chain incomplete or the client rejecting chain ordering. Since it worked before, likely our deployed bundle is missing intermediate.
Sam K: Pulled the bundle from rotator storage — two PEM blocks (leaf + root). Intermediate missing. Rotator should assemble leaf+intermediate+root. Hypothesis: customer intermediate had CRLF or was mangled by their CI so our parser skipped it.
Jeff L: Repro locally:
```
# current (bad) bundle
openssl x509 -in bad-bundle.pem -noout -text | grep "Subject:"
# shows only CN=api.private.acme.internal and CN=Acme Root CA
wc -c bad-bundle.pem -> 3256
```
Sam K: Root cause theory: their CI ran a cleanup that removed BEGIN/END markers (e.g., `sed -i 's/\r$//'` misused) and rotator ignored the intermediate. That left a leaf-only chain — clients that require full chain fail the handshake.
Oncall Bot: @pri oncall assigned
Priya R: Actions: 1) Ask customer to re-upload full PEM including intermediate (we'll provide exact commands). 2) Re-run rotator or rollback to previous known-good bundle (sha: b7f4c3) if needed. 3) Add rotator validations to prevent this.
Jeff L: Commands to verify/fix before re-upload:
```
# verify BEGIN/END present
awk '/BEGIN/,/END/ {print}' intermediate.pem | sed -n '1p; $p'
# assemble bundle
cat leaf.pem intermediate.pem root.pem > full-bundle.pem
# verify chain locally
openssl verify -CAfile root.pem full-bundle.pem
# quick smoke against endpoint
openssl s_client -connect api.private.acme.internal:443 -showcerts < /dev/null
```
AcmeOps: We'll check our CI and re-upload. Also: how will you detect truncated uploads in future?
Sam K: Logged INF-2142 to add bundle sanity checks: cert-count and size heuristics, fail-early on missing intermediate.
Priya R: Scheduling rollback in 10m; if customer uploads full bundle within 15m we abort rollback and re-run rotation.
Jeff L: Also adding automated post-rotation smoke: from a VPC node run s_client and assert chain length >=3 before marking job success.
AcmeOps: Uploaded full-bundle.tar.gz via console at 02:22 UTC. We kept the intermediate and ensured UNIX line endings.
Sam K: Re-run at 02:24 UTC. New bundle size 8.6KB. Rotator logs: "bundle validated: 3 certs, posted to edge, reload success".
AcmeOps: Confirmed — no more handshake errors, traffic normal. Thanks :tada: 
Priya R: Postmortem items: rotator validations + clearer upload errors to customers, docs update (how to preserve BEGIN/END and verify with openssl), and a support troubleshooting checklist for chain problems.
Oncall Bot: Incident closed by Priya R at 02:42 UTC
Sam K: Closing thread as resolved. Will link INF-2142 when ready.
